Why evaluate

## In a world of scarce resources, you need evidence on what is actually worth funding

The EU is one of the world's largest investors in innovation, yet significant regional
disparities in innovation outcomes are limiting its overall competitiveness. To remain
on par with global counterparts, every euro invested needs to yield greater returns and
have a more substantial impact on growth.

The processes behind these investments often lack mechanisms for continuous learning,
even as policy needs to keep adapting to evolving circumstances. This calls for
identifying challenges, testing solutions, and refining approaches.

::: {.gold-panel}
This is what we call **science-based adaptive delivery**: testing, learning, and
adjusting as you go.
:::

## Testing and learning only works if you know what to look for

When evaluating projects, we often only assess outputs, because they are the easiest
thing to count. Impact evaluation is what lets you move from measuring outputs to
proving outcomes.

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
#### Outputs
What a program delivers: grants disbursed, firms enrolled, trainings run.
:::
::: {.card-e}
#### Outcomes
What changes because of it: growth, jobs, innovation, resilience.
:::
:::

To understand in advance why each step should lead to the next, you need to map out,
before implementation, how a program's activities are expected to change the problem
you are addressing. That causal logic, the how and why behind each step, explains a
program's reason for existing, and tells you what to measure to test whether the
expected change is actually happening.

::: {.chain}
::: {.step}
**Inputs**
:::
::: {.step}
**Activities**
:::
::: {.step}
**Outputs**
:::
::: {.on}
**Outcomes**
:::
:::

This chain is the foundation of a Theory of Change, and having thought it through helps
in designing a strong impact evaluation. There is more on this in
[Why and When](01-why-and-when.qmd).

::: {.eyebrow}
What is an impact evaluation
:::

## But what is impact evaluation exactly?

::: {.gold-panel}
It allows us to answer the questions: what impact did this intervention have on regional
development, and how did different approaches change the outcome? For whom did it work
best, and under which conditions?
:::

To answer that, an impact evaluation isolates a program's actual effect from everything
else going on (economic trends, other policies, or the kinds of firms likely to apply in
the first place), rather than just describing what happened. It compares what actually
happened after introducing a program to what would have happened without it, the
counterfactual.

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
#### Not the same as M&E
M&E tracks whether a program is implemented as planned. Impact evaluation tests whether
it caused a real difference, compared to what would have happened without it.
:::
::: {.card-e}
#### Built in from day one
The comparison group, sample size, and data collection all depend on decisions made
before a program launches, not added on afterward.
:::
::: {.card-e}
#### Each one builds on the last
Each evaluation answers some questions and raises new ones, helping you understand your
regional market and design more impactful programs next time.
:::
:::
